title: Ireland 20-17 South Africa: Irish edge past world champions in Nations Championship thriller
html:
Highlights: Ireland 20-17 South Africa

  • Published

Nations Championship

Ireland (17) 20

Tries: Baloucoune 2, Kelleher Con: Prendergast Pen: Prendergast

South Africa (10) 17

Try: Van den Berg, Marx Cons: Feinberg-Mngomezulu 2 Pens: Feinberg-Mngomezulu

Ireland exacted revenge on world champions South Africa with a thrilling win in Dublin after England's victory over New Zealand dashed Andy Farrell's side's hopes of reaching next weekend's Nations Championship final.

With banned South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus hosting a watchalong stream from his team's hotel, the Springboks fell to back-to-back Test defeats for the first time since November 2022 after last week's loss to France in Paris.

A losing bonus-point, however, is enough for South Africa to top the southern hemisphere table and secure a place in the final against France, who beat Argentina 45-17 later on Saturday.

Ireland, who were shown five cards during last year's 24-13 loss to the Springboks in Dublin, led at the break after two tries from Robert Baloucoune and a Ronan Kelleher score, with Morne van den Berg crossing for the visitors.

After Canan Moodie had a try ruled out early in the second half, Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast - who was cleared to play by a disciplinary panel earlier this week - stretched Ireland's lead with a penalty.

However, hooker Malcolm Marx's 57th-minute try hauled South Africa back into it before yellow cards for Ireland captain Dan Sheehan and Springbok replacement Marco van Staden - the latter upgraded to red - set up a nail-biting denouement in the final 10 minutes.

But amid a hair-raising atmosphere inside Aviva Stadium, Ireland held on for a much-needed win after six successive double-digit defeats by the Springboks, New Zealand and France.

France's win meant that Ireland had to settle for third place in the table, and they will face Australia in a fifth-place play-off at Twickenham on Friday at 20:10 GMT.

Ireland narrowly beat Australia 33-31 in Sydney in July, but the Wallabies have since had a change of head coach after Les Kiss replaced Joe Schmidt.

Ireland front up to SA after Erasmus-dominated build-up

Robert Baloucoune (14) scored two first-half tries for Ireland

After an explosive build-up headlined by Erasmus, who was banned for six matches on Tuesday after questioning the integrity of match officials in last week's game against France, Saturday's contest in Dublin had a lot to live up to.

But it delivered emphatically during a breathless first half as Ireland fronted up impressively to South Africa's immense physicality.

In last year's meeting in Dublin, Ireland ended a nightmarish first half with 12 players on the field as South Africa - and their mighty scrum - played the game on their terms.

Fuelled by the pain of that encounter, Ireland attacked the game with real gusto and while South Africa fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicked the first points of the game, Ireland bossed possession and territory for much of the opening half.

There were plenty of moments for the sold-out crowd to cheer, with perhaps the biggest roar reserved for the hosts winning a rare scrum penalty after 26 minutes.

Baloucoune was exceptional, too. In addition to faring well in the aerial battle, the rapid Ulster wing displayed his finishing skills to get Ireland on the board, slipping past Damian Willemse and touching down after being picked out by Stuart McCloskey.

While Baloucoune - who also crossed twice against Fiji last week - was denied a second try by a superb piece of last-ditch defending by Springbok number eight Cameron Hanekom, Joe McCarthy won a turnover to deny the visitors momentum.

From there, Ireland kicked to the corner and eventually worked the ball back to Baloucoune on the right, who dived over in the corner for his second.

But with both conversion attempts missed by Prendergast, Ireland were pegged back when South Africa won a penalty inside green territory, with Van den Berg dotting down off the back of a scrum.

Unlike last year, though, Ireland had the final say of the half and restored their lead when Kelleher scored off a well-worked line-out.

In a bizarre twist, banned South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus hosted a watchalong of the game from the team's Dublin hotel

South Africa's frustration deepened early in the second half when Moodie's fine finish in the corner was ruled out after the replacement back was pushed into touch by Mack Hansen.

Ireland pulled further clear when Prendergast atoned for his missed kicks at goal with a penalty to put the hosts 20-10 up.

But after world player of the year Marx forced his way over with more than 20 minutes remaining, Ireland were denied a fourth try when Sheehan - in his first Test start at number eight - was held up on the line.

Sheehan was then yellow-carded at the same time as Van Staden, for a croc roll and dangerous clear-out respectively, and while South Africa pushed for a late winner, Ireland held on for a statement win.

Reacting from what looked like a conference room at his team's hotel, Erasmus slammed a table in frustration at full-time before his stream ended, spelling a miserable end to a tumultuous week for the two-time World Cup-winning coach.

Line-ups

Ireland: Keenan; Baloucoune, Henshaw, McCloskey, Hansen; Prendergast, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong, McCarthy, Beirne, Baird, Van der Flier, Sheehan (capt)

Replacements: Stewart, O'Toole, Clarkson, Ryan, Timoney, Casey, Frawley, Aki

Sin-bin: Sheehan (73)

South Africa: Willemse; Arendse, Kriel, De Allende, Hooker; Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Van den Berg; Nche, Marx, Louw, Etzebeth, Mostert, Kolisi (capt), PS du Toit, Hanekom

Replacements: Wessels, Steenekamp, T du Toit, De Jager, De Villiers, Van Staden, Williams, Moodie

Sent-off: Van Staden (73)

Match officials

Referee: C Ridley (RFU)

Assistant referees: A Gardner (RA) & A Woodthorpe (RFU)

Television match official: I Tempest (RFU)

Foul play review officer: T Trainini (FFR)
summary: Ireland exact revenge on world champions South Africa with a thrilling win in Dublin after England's victory over New Zealand dashes Andy Farrell's side's hopes of reaching next weekend's Nations Championship final.
